newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS could raise prices on some routes.
newsitem.headline: SAS could raise prices on some routes.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Thursday that its dominant position on some routes allowed it raise prices to compensate for reductions forced upon it by competition elsewhere.
Speaking to reporters at a seminar in the Danish capital SAS director Vagn Soerensen would not specify which routes or how by much fares could rise.
"Prices in general will fall, but our slightly peripheral position in Europe also gives us the opportunity to raise fares," he said.
"That gives us something to fight back with."

Soerensen said that 18 percent of the carrier's available seats in Scandinavia had no competitor while 53 percent shared routes with one other operator and only 29 percent had to fight for market share with two or more rivals.
SAS is owned jointly by the Danish, Norwegian and Swedish govenments and private investors.

It earlier anounced a broad programme of temporary and longer-term fare reductions on its Copenhagen-Stockholm route to counter competition from Maersk Air, part of the powerful A.P. Moeller shipping group. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom + 45 33969650
